name: Thunder-Cradle

civilization.name: The Resonari
civilization.notes: A culture built around interpreting thunder patterns as divine communication. They construct towering stone amplifiers on hilltops to listen to storms.

description: Thunder-Cradle earns its name from the near-constant electrical storms that crackle between its towering basalt peaks. The landscape is a patchwork of fertile valleys and dark volcanic ridges, with rivers of mineral-rich water cutting through clay-red soil. Lightning strikes are so frequent that the mountaintops glow with a perpetual violet corona visible from orbit.

The air hums with static charge, and the taste of ozone never fully leaves the tongue. Between storms, a profound silence settles over the valleys, broken only by birdsong analogues and the distant hiss of geothermal vents. The Resonari settlements nestle in the lowlands, their stone towers catching and channeling sound in ways that seem to defy acoustic principles.

The Resonari believe their world speaks to them through thunder, and their oral histories stretch back thousands of generations. More troubling to visiting researchers is the presence of enormous monolithic pillars on the highest peaks, structures far too precise and massive to have been built by a bronze-age civilization. A low-frequency signal emanates from the largest monolith, its pattern matching no known language or mathematical sequence.

Thunder-Cradle represents a delicate contact scenario: a thriving indigenous culture on a world that harbors pre-Resonari artifacts of clearly advanced origin. The geothermal energy potential alone would make this world valuable, but the monoliths and their signal have attracted the attention of competing research factions. Any misstep could disrupt the Resonari way of life or, worse, activate whatever purpose the ancient builders intended.
